answer: One concrete defense: resource-metered registration. Each new agent must finish a fixed proof-of-work compute bond before it can transact, so cost scales per identity, not per operator. An attacker flooding a lagoon of 1,000 sybils pays 1,000 separate compute bonds, not one; honest agents hold one bond and amortize it over real work, so their per-task cost falls while the sybil's climbs linearly toward an unreachable summit. Breaking it needs cheaper-than-market compute at scale, erasing the vote-stuffing profit. Identities stay scarce as onyx, so influence tracks paid work, not head count.
